_metadata.description: Roadmap #3 Phase 1 — first real-model swap-counter validation
_metadata.hardware: RunPod A100 80GB PCIe (NVIDIA driver via runpod/pytorch)
_metadata.vllm_log_corroboration: Sequence group streaming_chat_32k_2 is preempted by PreemptionMode.SWAP mode because there is not enough KV cache space. ... total_num_cumulative_preemption=1
what_this_proves: AsyncLLMEngine + preemption_mode='swap' actually engages the swap path under sustained Pareto-bursty load on a real model.
The audit-fix list-of-tuples parser (commit 9ba827a) correctly counts swap events on vLLM 0.7's CpuGpuBlockAllocator. Without that fix the value would be 0.
Roadmap #3 Phase 1's design is sound: streaming async submission + tuned KV budget produces real swap counters.

The hyperparameters that engage swap on Qwen 7B + A100 80GB: GPU_MEM_UTIL=0.26 (KV ~1.91 GiB; concurrency at 32K = 1.09x), arrival_rate=6/sec, max_decode_tokens=2048, prompt-length distribution biased to 8K-30K.
what_this_does_not_prove: CTM+ vs LRU policy effect on a real model — this is LRU only (Phase 1).
That CTM+ would beat LRU under these conditions — Phase 2 is gated on the modern-vLLM allocator-evictor patch.
Multi-cell / multi-seed / multi-workload reproducibility — single cell only.
That this swap-engagement regime matches any specific partner workload — it is a synthetic stress pattern designed to force preemption.
next_steps_gated_on_partner_request: Multi-cell sweep (3 workloads x 3 seeds with these tuned params, ~30 min, ~$0.60 GPU spot).
Phase 2 implementation: CTM+ allocator-evictor patch on modern vLLM, ~2 days code + GPU validation.
